subject: Private deployment: key custody, subprocessors, and dataflow mapping
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@clinix.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Clinix Legal <legal@clinix.io>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: Private deployment — key custody + subprocessors questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to follow up with a few gating questions before we can progress the SOW for a VPC/private deployment: 

1) BYOK / Customer keys: can Clinix bring and fully control the KMS keys (CMEK)? Will Redwood require key escrow or any form of access to the plaintext key for support?
2) Subprocessors: can you provide the current list and confirm any planned third-party access to the private deployment control plane or operator services?
3) Operator access / break-glass: what are the exact conditions under which Redwood personnel can access the environment (if at all)? Is access logged/audited and limited to specific roles?
4) Cross-border and data transfers: our legal team needs a dataflow map showing any flows that leave the EU and any subprocessors involved in those flows.
5) Evidence: we need SOC2+, minimal telemetry examples, and a sample DPA redline to circulate internally.

Procurement timebox: we need answers and a DPA redline by close of day Jan 20 to hit internal review cycles. Is that feasible?

Appreciate a brief written response + any artifacts you can share. If easier, happy to set a quick call.

Best,
Marta Lopez
Head of IT Operations
Clinix Health

(attachment: procurement_requirements.pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@clinix.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 13:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Private deployment — key custody + subprocessors questions

Hi Marta,

Thanks — and great to hear procurement is moving this along. Quick answers up front, and Rishi/Karthik are looped for detail and artifacts.

1) BYOK/CMEK: Yes — we support customer-managed keys (we integrate with customer KMS via external key references). Customers retain cryptographic control; Redwood never stores plaintext customer keys. We do offer an optional, customer-authorized key-escrow flow for on-prem installers (HSM-to-HSM transfer) but it is purely optional and requires a separate contractual addendum.

2) Subprocessors: We will provide a current subprocessor inventory. For private/VPC deployments the set is intentionally small (monitoring & software support agents in the control plane). Any operator access is via ephemeral sessions tied to explicit incidents; no persistent backend access to customer data.

3) Operator access / break-glass: Operator access is limited to named roles, can be scoped to specific namespaces, requires 2-person approval, and is fully logged with immutable audit trails. Break-glass requires runbook-triggered approvals and is time-boxed.

4) Cross-border transfers: We can produce a dataflow diagram showing any egress paths. For typical EU deployments we keep all tenant data in-region; auxiliary telemetry (aggregated, non-PII) may be routed to central observability regions for platform health, but this can be configured off by request.

5) Evidence & DPA: Attached is a redline of our standard DPA to get you started (Redlined_DPA_Clinix_v1.docx). Rishi will share SOC2 artifact examples and the current subprocessor CSV. Karthik will share a draft dataflow map and links to controls.

We can get everything to you by Jan 16 so you have time for internal review before the 20th. Would you like a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk procurement/legal through the key points?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

(attachment: Redlined_DPA_Clinix_v1.docx)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 10:24:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Private deployment — key custody + subprocessors questions

Marta / Marissa — adding a bit more technical specificity (pasting suggested contract language in-line for ease):

- BYOK / Key custody (sample clause): 
"Customer owns and retains exclusive control of Customer Managed Keys (CMKs). Redwood shall not require access to plaintext CMKs to provide service. Any requested operator access to encrypted material will be performed using cryptographic operations provided by the Customer's KMS endpoints; Redwood will not export, copy, or persist plaintext keying material."

- Optional escrow (summary): If permitted by the customer, Redwood can provide an HSM-based escrow mechanism where keys are sealed under a dual-control policy and released only with written customer authorization or under a court order following the process described in Appendix B. We treat escrow as an add-on; default deployment does not use escrow.

- Subprocessor limitation (sample clause): 
"For Private Deployments, Redwood will limit subprocessors to those necessary for control-plane orchestration and telemetry ingestion. Redwood will provide a current subprocessor list upon execution and will provide 30 days' notice of material changes. Redwood personnel will not have direct access to tenant application data in the customer's environment absent explicit, time-boxed, logged, two-person approved break-glass events."

- Telemetry examples: We can offer a minimal telemetry profile that sends only aggregate platform metrics (CPU, memory, request counts) and no request payloads or model outputs. Detailed audit logs (operator session records, commands executed) are exportable to the customer's SIEM for retention.

I've attached the current subprocessor inventory we would share with customers (subprocessors_20260112.csv). Also happy to provide sample SOC2 audit reports and evidence packs under an NDA.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Privacy, Redwood Inference

(attachment: subprocessors_20260112.csv)

Hi Marta — attaching the requested dataflow diagram and a short deployment runbook that shows where telemetry can be toggled off. Highlights: 

- For Clinix's EU region deployment we plan to keep compute, storage, and model weights in-region; no model input/output leaves the EU in the default configuration.
- Control-plane connectors (for Redwoods' control plane to push updates) can be configured to operate over an air-gapped relay inside the customer's VPC; we can also provide a full on-prem control-plane option if required.
- Break-glass confirmation: Operator access requires two-person approval (one engineering lead + one security approver); every session is recorded and audit trails are exported in real-time to the customer's SIEM endpoint (Syslog/HTTPS).

Attachments: dataflow_map_clinix.pdf, deployment_runbook_excerpt.txt
Docusign: Executable DPA & SOW link: https://app.docusign.com/XYZ-CLX-DPA-2026
Shared artefacts: https://drive.redwood.company/clinix/dpa-evidence

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
